articles.description: Spaniard wins final 6-2, 7-6 (7) against new world No 1 Alcaraz the fourth to win career grand slam and ATP Finals The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time. So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year. Continue reading...

articles.description: The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight. Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly. Continue reading...

articles.title: Max Verstappen claims dramatic Las Vegas F1 GP win after Ferraris collide
articles.description: Dutchman under siege before pulling clear in the final lap Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton again clash on track For a race still in its infancy, this year’s Las Vegas Grand Prix provided a spectacle for the ages. The victory for Max Verstappen once more exemplified why he must be acknowledged as one of the greats of Formula One after a compelling race-long battle where the lead changed 34 times but on every occasion, and most important on the last lap, it was the Red Bull driver who had his nose in front. This was a race unique to this season and not seen in the sport for a long time, an old-school duel of slipstreaming and the sort of over-the-top extravaganza perfect for Las Vegas, Cirque du Soleil fashioned from carbon fibre and noise. Continue reading...
